title: Orbital angular momentum in crystalline solids: non-equilibrium theory
authors: Sangeeta Sharma, Peter Elliott, Samuel Shallcross
abstract: We develop a general operator theory of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in periodic solids that applies equally to equilibrium and coherently driven states. Employing the crystal momentum representation of Adams and Blount, we construct a periodic-solid OAM operator exactly corresponding to the symmetrized $\hat{\mathbf r}\times\hat{\mathbf v}$ observable, and show that it separates into local circulation (LC) and itinerant circulation (IC) sectors that are Hermitian and $U(1)$, and more generally $U(N)$, gauge covariant. In equilibrium, the LC and IC sectors reduce to the established modern theory of orbital magnetism; out of equilibrium, the same operator structure exposes new contributions generated by laser-written momentum-space textures and interband coherence. Applied to gapped graphene, we uncover a rich phenomenology of ultrafast non-equilibrium orbital angular momentum, including a quasi-stationary light-induced OAM. This latter finding, underpinned by a close connection between band-manifold phase texture and nonequilibrium OAM, points towards new possibilities for light control over OAM in solids as well as a potentially rich role for topological band structures in designed OAM materials.
summary: This work establishes a unified operator theory for Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) in crystalline solids, applicable across both steady-state and ultrafast non-equilibrium regimes. By decomposing OAM into local and itinerant components, the authors predict that external driving fields, such as intense lasers, can generate novel, quasi-stationary OAM signatures linked to momentum-space phase structures. This opens new avenues for controlling light-matter interactions using topological properties of band structures.
main_problem: To develop a general operator theory for Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) in periodic solids that remains valid for both equilibrium and non-equilibrium states.
main_result: The theory successfully decomposes OAM into local and itinerant circulation sectors, revealing new non-equilibrium contributions from momentum-space phase textures when driven by light.
method: The authors employ the crystal momentum representation (CMR) of Adams and Blount to construct the OAM operator, decomposing it into covariant derivative and dipole matrix terms.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to crystalline solids, with specific calculations performed for gapped graphene. The formalism relies on band structure analysis and the decomposition of position and velocity operators.
key_observables: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), Local Circulation (LC) and Itinerant Circulation (IC) sectors, Berry curvature, and quasi-stationary light-induced OAM.
important_parameters: Equilibrium vs. non-equilibrium driving conditions, laser-written momentum-space textures, and band manifold phase texture.
main_assumptions: The use of the crystal momentum representation (CMR) is crucial to circumvent issues with the position operator in the standard Bloch representation.
paper_structure: The paper builds the OAM operator using CMR, separates it into LC and IC sectors, derives the equilibrium limit matching existing theory, and then extends the framework to analyze non-equilibrium dynamics using phase texture analysis.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between light-induced momentum-space phase textures and measurable, quasi-stationary OAM provides a concrete, controllable mechanism for manipulating angular momentum in solid-state systems, relevant to quantum optics and light-matter interaction.
